svg.text: Hang the shaft: drive FIXED, idler on the micro-adjust plate
One bearing defines the axis; the other adjusts parallelism and lets the shaft grow.

Grey = already built · colour = this step
Transfer the bearing bolt pattern FROM THE BEARING YOU BOUGHT onto P-001L and P-023.
Do not drill from the drawing — that pattern is an assumption.
Slide the 24″ shaft through the drum and both panels, then set the H-029 clamp
Bolt H-001 to the drive side and torque it. That bearing is now DATUM-E, the
Pin P-023 to the idler side with H-032, mount H-002 on it, and set the H-030 jack
screw against P-024. Snug the bearing only — the shaft must still slide axially
Spin the drum by hand through several turns. It should coast, not bind and not ring.

Shaft turns freely; measurable axial float at the idler end;
jack screw makes contact with a witness mark.

⚠ Locking both bearings bends the shaft and kills both of
them. Do not do it because it feels tighter.
